## Exploratory data analysis

The provided dataset consists of a four-dimensional array containing 25,000 images of handwritten digits, along with associated metadata. Each image has a resolution of 28 x 28 pixels and contains a single channel representing greyscale intensity. The five digits from 0 - 4 were each written 50 times by 20 different individuals during each of the five independent sessions. The array contains no missing values, indicating all images and associated metadata were complete. Pixel values ranged from 0, indicating a blank background, to 255, representing a pixel with maximal intensity. 

Variation arose between individuals in several ways (@fig-inter-ind_var), including differences in digit size, particularly for the digit '0'. As shown in (@fig-inter-ind_var), individuals 3 and 12 had much smaller '0's than individuals 1, 10, and 16. The angle and curvature of strokes also varied. For example, the vertical stroke in digit '1' was straight for individual 1, more curved for individual 3 and straight but more diagonal for individual 10. Similarly, the diagonal and vertical strokes in digit '4' varied in angle and curvature across individuals. The digit '0' also tilted in different directions for individuals 10 and 12 compared to 1,3, and 16 (@fig-inter-ind_var). 

Although inter-individual variation was more pronounced, variation was still observed within individuals, both across sessions (@fig-within-ind-var) and within a given session (@fig-within-ind-var-single-session). Repeated samples of a given digit by the same individual tended to be similar in size. However, some variation once again arose in the angle and curvature of strokes, such as the top-right corner of the digit '0' and the angle of the bottom horizontal stroke of the digit '2' (@fig-within-ind-var). 

Intra-individual variation was more apparent across different sessions than within the same session. For individual 16, the bottom stroke of the digit '2' was more consistent across samples in the same session than across different sessions. Within the same individual and session, there was more variation in pixel intensity, as illustrated by the bottom horizontal stroke of the digit '1' (@fig-within-ind-var-single-session). 

There are several visible limitations to the simulated handwritten digit data. First, some digits contain unusually straight lines and sharp angles in digits where these are unlikely to occur in natural handwriting. An example is the top-right corner of the digit '0' for individual 10 (@fig-inter-ind_var). Second, line continuity is sometimes interrupted, as seen in the gaps in the digit '2' across sessions 3, 4 and 5 for individual 16 (@fig-within-ind-var) and in all selected samples for digit '2' from session 1 (@fig-within-ind-var-single-session). 

Furthermore, the simulated data does not capture variation in stroke thickness that would arise from variable pressure during real-world writing. There is also limited variation in digit style; for example, the digit '1' can be written as a single vertical line, which is not represented in the simulated data. In some cases, the simulated data also appears unrealistic. For instance, individual 3's digit '1' which closely resembles a '2', making it difficult to identify the intended digit.

```{r}
#| label: data_exploration
#| eval: false

# Actual 'images'
class(handwriting$images) # array containing images
str(handwriting) # split into images themselves and metadata for images 
dim(handwriting$images) # 25000 images each 28 by 28 pixels and a single channel
handwriting$images[1,1:28,1:28,1] # example of single image
anyNA(handwriting$images) # no NA values within any of the images

# Scale of pixels (values within images)
str(handwriting$image_scale)
summary(handwriting$image_scale) # ranges from 0 (background) to 255 (maximum ink)

# Metadata
class(handwriting$metadata) # data frame containing metadata
str(handwriting$metadata)
summary(handwriting$metadata) 
# 20 people, 5 sessions, 5 digits, 50 replicates per digit per person per session = 25 000
head(handwriting$metadata)
anyNA(handwriting$metadata)

```

```{r}
#| label: fig-inter-ind_var
#| fig-cap: "Handwritten digits for four randomly selected individuals indicating inter-individual variability within a single session (Session 1, Samples 1)."
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 5

# Randomly select a session and four people 
set.seed(99)
people <- sample(20, 5, replace = FALSE) %>% sort()

# Get IDs for plotting examples across people and digits for a single session
image_id1 <- handwriting$metadata %>% 
  filter(session == 1, # session 1 only
         replicate == 1, # replicate 1 only
         person_id %in% people) %>% # only first 5 people as samples
  select(image_id) %>%
  pull() # extract the image ids as list of integers

# Create a data frame from array data for plotting
samples <- expand.grid(image_id = image_id1, row = 1:28, column = 1:28)  %>% # empty matrix with specific image_ids
  left_join(handwriting$metadata %>% select(image_id, person_id, digit))
samples$value <- as.vector(handwriting$images[image_id1,,,]) # add pixel scale values

samples %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = column, y = row, fill = value)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "black") + # colour pixels by scale value
  scale_y_reverse() + # flip to correct orientation
  coord_equal(expand = FALSE) + # same height and width of pixels
  scale_x_continuous(position = "top") + # Move x axis label to the top
  facet_grid(person_id ~ digit, switch = "y") + # person by rows, digits by columns
  theme_void() + # remove formatting then re-add where necessary below
  theme(legend.position = "none", # remove legend
        panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey", fill = NA, size = 0.5), # outline each of the drawings
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "lightgrey", size = 0.5), # boxes for x and y axis labels
        strip.text.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 5, t = 5)), # x axis labels
        strip.text.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", angle = 0, margin = margin(r = 5, l = 5)), # y axis labels
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 13, margin = margin(t = 5, b = 5)), # x axis title 
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 13, margin = margin(r = 5, l = 5), angle = 90) # y axis title
        ) +
  labs(x = "Digit", y = "Person")

```

```{r}
#| label: fig-within-ind-var
#| fig-cap: "Handwritten digits for a single randomly selected individual (Person 16) from five different sessions (all Sample 1) indicating within-individual variability across sessions."
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 5

# Randomly select an individual
set.seed(99)
person <- sample(20, 1)

# Get IDs for plotting examples for one person across sessions and digits
image_id2 <- handwriting$metadata %>% 
  filter(replicate == 1, # replicate 1 only
         person_id == person) %>% # randomly selected person 
  select(image_id) %>%
  pull() # extract the image ids as list of integers

# Create a data frame from array data for plotting
samples <- expand.grid(image_id = image_id2, row = 1:28, column = 1:28)  %>% # empty matrix with specific image_ids
  left_join(handwriting$metadata %>% select(image_id, session, digit))
samples$value <- as.vector(handwriting$images[image_id2,,,]) # add pixel scale values

samples %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = column, y = row, fill = value)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "black") + # colour pixels by scale value
  scale_y_reverse() + # flip to correct orientation
  coord_equal(expand = FALSE) + # same height and width of pixels
  scale_x_continuous(position = "top") + # Move x axis label to the top
  facet_grid(session ~ digit, switch = "y") + # person by rows, digits by columns
  theme_void() + # remove formatting then re-add where necessary below
  theme(legend.position = "none", # remove legend
        panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey", fill = NA, size = 0.5), # outline each of the drawings
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "lightgrey", size = 0.5), # boxes for x and y axis labels
        strip.text.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 5, t = 5)), # x axis labels
        strip.text.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", angle = 0, margin = margin(r = 5, l = 5)), # y axis labels
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 13, margin = margin(t = 5, b = 5)), # x axis title 
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 13, margin = margin(r = 5, l = 5), angle = 90) # y axis title
        ) +
  labs(x = "Digit", y = "Session")

```

```{r}
#| label: fig-within-ind-var-single-session
#| fig-cap: "Handwritten digits for a single randomly selected individual (Person 16) from five random samples within a single session (Session 1) indicating within-individual variability within a session"
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 5

# Randomly select samples
set.seed(99)
samples <- sample(50, 5, replace = FALSE) %>% sort()

# Get IDs for plotting examples for one person across sessions and digits
image_id3 <- handwriting$metadata %>% 
  filter(session == 1,
         replicate %in% samples, # random samples
         person_id == person) %>% # randomly selected person 
  select(image_id) %>%
  pull() # extract the image ids as list of integers

# Create a data frame from array data for plotting
samples <- expand.grid(image_id = image_id3, row = 1:28, column = 1:28)  %>% # empty matrix with specific image_ids
  left_join(handwriting$metadata %>% select(image_id, replicate, digit))
samples$value <- as.vector(handwriting$images[image_id3,,,]) # add pixel scale values

samples %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = column, y = row, fill = value)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "black") + # colour pixels by scale value
  scale_y_reverse() + # flip to correct orientation
  coord_equal(expand = FALSE) + # same height and width of pixels
  scale_x_continuous(position = "top") + # Move x axis label to the top
  facet_grid(replicate ~ digit, switch = "y") + # person by rows, digits by columns
  theme_void() + # remove formatting then re-add where necessary below
  theme(legend.position = "none", # remove legend
        panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey", fill = NA, size = 0.5), # outline each of the drawings
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "lightgrey", size = 0.5), # boxes for x and y axis labels
        strip.text.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 5, t = 5)), # x axis labels
        strip.text.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", angle = 0, margin = margin(r = 5, l = 5)), # y axis labels
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 13, margin = margin(t = 5, b = 5)), # x axis title 
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 13, margin = margin(r = 5, l = 5), angle = 90) # y axis title
        ) +
  labs(x = "Digit", y = "Replicate")

```
